solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Habit singles developed getting settled?

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notices that single people's routines evolve as they settle down into domestic life.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish oneself is to become settled in a place or role, so the present participle describes getting settled.

clue.text: Foreigners in Michigan cutting cloth from the South

indicators.note: Michigan's letters cut into the cloth, sitting inside it
in a down clue, read from the south means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing twilled cloth
MI is the postal abbreviation for Michigan

explanation.surface: Immigrants in Michigan are snipping fabric that came from the southern states.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'from the South' means read upwards, from the bottom of the column.
explanation.definitionFit: Emigres are people who have left their own country, often for political reasons, so they are foreigners where they settle.

clue.text: Take to the floor in time and almost start moving

indicators.note: almost means the word and loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before shortening
to go is to start moving

explanation.surface: A dancer joins the floor on the beat, just about beginning to move.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance, and to dance it is to take to the dance floor.

clue.text: None of these graduates has any Dutch

definitions.text: None of these graduates has any Dutch

parts.words: None of these graduates has any Dutch
parts.note: graduates holding a first degree share this name with unmarried men, and 'Dutch' is old cockney slang for a wife, as in 'my old Dutch'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' looks like the language, but in cockney 'my old Dutch' is one's wife; the graduates with first degrees are also men without wives.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both holders of a first university degree and unmarried men, who by definition have no wife.

clue.text: Some Asians lacking help in retirement hostels

indicators.note: lacking means the letters for help are removed from the Asians

parts.note: Indians are some of the peoples of Asia

indicators.note: something in retirement withdraws, so the word for help is read backwards

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Some Asian travellers without assistance end up staying in hostels when they retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' turns AID into DIA, and 'lacking' removes DIA from INDIANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Inns are public houses offering lodging to travellers, much as hostels offer cheap accommodation.

clue.text: High-Churchman in Paris yesterday on a bender

parts.note: hier is French for yesterday, as said in Paris
an arch is something bent into a curve

explanation.surface: A senior cleric in Paris was out drinking heavily the day before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bender' looks like a drinking spree, but here it is something that bends: an ARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A hierarch is a chief priest or senior figure in a church hierarchy, a high-ranking churchman.

clue.text: Inventor, not a telephone man, giving away all at the end

parts.note: no means not

indicators.note: giving away means a letter is shed from the phrase before it

parts.note: Alexander Graham Bell is credited with inventing the telephone

indicators.note: at the end picks out the final letter of the word all

explanation.surface: An inventor who is not the telephone pioneer gave away his whole fortune at his death.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to the real Nobel leaving his fortune to found the prizes. NO BELL gives away L, the last letter of 'all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel was the Swedish chemist who invented dynamite and endowed the Nobel prizes.

clue.text: I am one term at sea

definitions.text: I am one term at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A speaker introduces themselves as a word relating to the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description: this word is one term for things at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime means connected with the sea and seafaring, so it is a term for things at sea.

clue.text: Old king's daughter throttling a president

indicators.note: throttling means gripping round the neck, so the daughter surrounds the letter

parts.note: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch's daughter is strangling a head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'old king' is Shakespeare's Lear, whose daughters were Goneril, Regan and Cordelia.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was the fortieth President of the United States.

clue.text: Artlessness of Connie dancing around enclosure

indicators.note: around means the rearranged name wraps the abbreviation
dancing letters move about, so the name is rearranged

parts.note: enc. is the standard abbreviation for enclosure in letters

explanation.surface: A naive girl called Connie dances round a paddock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enclosure' looks like a pen for animals, but here it is the abbreviation written at the foot of a business letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocence is a lack of guile or sophistication, which is what artlessness means.

clue.text: See red but initially do very little

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word but

parts.note: to laze is to do very little

explanation.surface: Become furious, but at first be idle.
explanation.definitionFit: To blaze can mean to burn with fierce anger, just as seeing red means flaring up in rage.

clue.text: Start afresh on work with finale requiring completion

parts.note: re means on, in the sense of concerning
op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: something requiring completion is unfinished, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the end is the finale

explanation.surface: A composer begins again on a piece whose final movement is still unwritten.
explanation.definitionFit: To reopen something is to begin it again after a pause, such as restarting a case or a business.

clue.text: Vital gun destroyed part of roof

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken apart, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A key artillery piece has wrecked a section of the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaulting is the arched masonry structure forming a ceiling or roof, as in a cathedral.

clue.text: Address issue besetting Exchange Rate Mechanism

indicators.note: besetting means surrounding on all sides, so the child encloses the abbreviation

parts.note: issue means offspring, such as a son
ERM is the abbreviation for the European Exchange Rate Mechanism

explanation.surface: A speech tackles a problem plaguing the European currency system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a problem, but here it means a child: a SON.
explanation.definitionFit: A sermon is a moral or religious talk delivered from the pulpit, a form of formal address.

clue.text: Instrument of justice

parts.note: looks like a gavel or the scales, but it is a woodwind instrument whose name is also a part-time judge in English courts

explanation.walkthrough: In England and Wales a Recorder is a barrister or solicitor sitting as a part-time judge, so the word is both a musical instrument and an agent of justice.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a simple woodwind pipe and also a part-time judge in the Crown Court.

clue.text: Poor little corporal is no stingy individual

indicators.note: poor means badly made here, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: Corp is the short form of corporal
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The unfortunate junior officer is not a mean person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little corporal' recalls Napoleon, but it only shortens the rank to CORP. 'Stingy' looks like miserly; here it means having a sting.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorpion is an arachnid with a venomous sting at the tip of its tail.

clue.text: Politician's behind naked pupil providing discipline in dining hall

indicators.note: behind means the politician comes after the stripped pupil
naked means stripped of its outer covering, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a prefect is a senior pupil who keeps order in a school
a Tory is a British Conservative politician; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A politician is behind a disciplinarian schoolchild who stripped off, in a canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A refectory is the communal dining room of a monastery, college or school.

clue.text: One group or another repressing resistance in part of UK

indicators.note: repressing means holding down inside, so the phrase encloses the letter

parts.note: some set means one group or another, no particular one
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Various factions suppress an uprising in a region of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is an English county in the south-west, so it is a part of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Support vessels going round barrier

parts.note: to back is to support

indicators.note: going round means turning about, so the word for vessels reads backwards

parts.note: pots are vessels

explanation.surface: Supporting ships sail around a blockade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' looks like the definition, but it is BACK; the definition is 'barrier'.
explanation.definitionFit: A backstop is a fence or screen behind a batter or a fallback safeguard, in either sense a barrier.

clue.text: Withdraw short order to look for Lamb's mistress

indicators.note: withdraw means draw back, so the shortened order reads backwards up the column
short means the order loses its last letter

parts.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire
to peep is to look

explanation.surface: Someone retreats from a brief command to have a look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts OBE to OB, and 'Withdraw' turns it to BO.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Bo-Peep is the nursery-rhyme shepherdess who lost her sheep, so she is mistress of the lambs.

clue.text: Result of Irons going head-to-head with first couple of actors chasing the lead?

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron; two of them meeting head to head gives one reversed against the other

indicators.note: first couple of keeps only the opening two letters of what is left
chasing away the lead removes the first letter of actors

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: Jeremy Irons faces off against a pair of leading actors chasing the starring role.
explanation.walkthrough: FE reversed meets FE nose to nose as EF FE. ACTORS with its lead A chased off is CTORS, whose first couple of letters are CT.
explanation.definitionFit: An effect is a consequence or outcome, the result of some cause.

clue.text: Stepmother malingering to keep warm

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the answer sits within these two words

explanation.surface: A stepmother pretends to be ill in order to stay cosy indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep warm' reads as one phrase, but 'to keep' signals the concealment and 'warm' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermal means relating to heat, and thermal clothing is designed to retain warmth.

clue.text: More than one function backing up rests after energy's lost

indicators.note: after means the rests come behind the reversed up
backing means moving in reverse, so the word up reads backwards
lost means the energy symbol is removed from the rests

parts.note: reposes are rests
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Something with several uses supports recuperation once a person's energy is exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns UP into PU, and REPOSES 'lost' E becomes RPOSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Purposes are aims or intended uses, so several of them are more than one function.

clue.text: Books containing most directions for assault

indicators.note: containing means the books hold the directions inside them

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible
three of the four compass points, north, south and east, are most of the directions

explanation.surface: Volumes holding nearly all the instructions for an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an attack or onslaught, as well as the beginning of something, so it means an assault.

clue.text: International line taken about London not right? It depends

indicators.note: not means the letter for right is left out

parts.note: the Circle line is a London Underground route running in a loop

explanation.surface: A traveller hopes an international route around London is going right, but it depends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It depends' seems to shrug, but 'depend' here means hang down, which an icicle does. The Circle line is a London Underground line.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle is a hanging spike of ice, and to depend in an old sense is to hang down.

clue.text: Several Roman figures start to back ascent

parts.note: C, L, I and M are each Roman numerals

indicators.note: start to means take the first letter of the word back

explanation.surface: Several Roman statues begin to support an uphill path.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb is an upward journey or slope, which is what an ascent is.

clue.text: Time of year unknown uncle from the States turns up?

parts.note: X is the algebraic symbol for an unknown quantity

indicators.note: turns up means flipped upwards, reading the name backwards in this down clue

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the United States

explanation.surface: At some point in the year a mysterious American relative arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' looks like arrives, but in a down clue it turns SAM upward to MAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Xmas is the short written form of Christmas, a festive season of the calendar.

clue.text: Fair chance of winning. Despite that, not finishing

indicators.note: not finishing means the phrase stops short of its last letter

parts.note: even so means despite that

explanation.surface: A punter judges the odds balanced, yet the race is unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, evens means odds of one to one, an equal chance of winning or losing.

clue.text: Classic party conference

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a drinking party in ancient Greece, famously the setting of Plato's dialogue
second meaning: a meeting where experts discuss a subject

explanation.walkthrough: 'Classic' points to classical Greece, where the word named a drinking party with conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an ancient Greek after-dinner drinking party and a modern academic meeting with talks.

clue.text: Data about classy sounding brass that's struck one is a sign of social rank

indicators.note: about means the data surround the upper-class letter

parts.note: stats, short for statistics, are data
U means upper-class in British usage

indicators.note: sounding means the brass instrument's name is said aloud as a similar word

parts.note: a cymbal is a brass percussion plate that is struck

explanation.surface: Statistics on the posh sound of a struck cymbal reveal a mark of prestige.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from 1950s British talk of U and non-U manners.
explanation.definitionFit: A status symbol is a possession taken to show wealth or prestige, an outward mark of social standing.
